## Findings
- claim-1: For \(v=v_{r,s,t,n}\), the associated rectangle is \(i^j\), with \(i=s-t+1\) and \(j=r-t+1\). [source-2@L1354-L1362|claim=formal-document]
- claim-2: The nonidentity bigrassmannians are parameterized by \(1\le t\le r,s\le n\) and \(t>r+s-n\), and \(v_{r,s,t,n}\) is explicitly the permutation in lines 987–991. [source-2@L973-L992|claim=formal-document]
- claim-3: Put \(q=n-r\). The inverse correspondence is \[ t=r-j+1,\qquad s=i+r-j,\qquad n=r+q. \] The source admissibility conditions are equivalent to \[ 1\le i\le q,\qquad1\le j\le r. \] Indeed, admissibility gives \(i,j\ge1\), \(j\le r\), and \(t>r+s-n\iff q-i+1>0\iff i\le q\). Conversely, these rectangle bounds give \(1\le t\le r\), \(t\le s<n\), and \(t-(r+s-n)=q-i+1>0\).
- claim-4: This correspondence is injective: from \((r,s,t,n)\), recover \((q,i,j)=(n-r,s-t+1,r-t+1)\); from \((r,q,i,j)\), recover \((r,s,t,n)\) by the preceding inverse formulas.
- claim-5: Each prescribed generating family has \(\binom{a+b}{a}\) elements, where \(a=\min(q-i,r-j)\) and \(b=\min(i,j)\). [source-2@L1382-L1421|claim=formal-document]
- claim-6: For nonempty rectangles, \(\binom{a+b}{a}>1\) exactly when \[ 1\le i\le q-1,\qquad1\le j\le r-1. \]
- claim-7: Under the convention \[ \{r\le5,\ q\le6\}\setminus\{r\le4,\ q\le5\}, \] the 90 deduplicated bigrassmannian instances with \(\binom{a+b}{a}>1\) are \[ v_{5,\,i+5-j,\,6-j,\,q+5}, \quad 2\le q\le6,\ 1\le i\le q-1,\ 1\le j\le4, \] giving \(4(1+2+3+4+5)=60\) cases, together with \[ v_{r,\,i+r-j,\,r-j+1,\,r+6}, \quad 2\le r\le4,\ 1\le i\le5,\ 1\le j\le r-1, \] giving \(5(1+2+3)=30\) cases. The two families are disjoint since their \(r\)-values are respectively \(5\) and \(2,3,4\); injectivity proves there are no further duplicates.
- claim-8: The paper reports computer verification of minimality only for \(r\le4\) and \(n-r\le5\). [source-2@L1495-L1502|claim=formal-document]
## Strategy
Use the source-backed formulas \(i=s-t+1\), \(j=r-t+1\), with \(q=n-r\). Prove the bijection only after retaining \((r,q)\):
\[
(r,s,t,n)\longleftrightarrow(r,q,i,j),
\quad
t=r-j+1,\ s=i+r-j,\ n=r+q.
\]
For \(r,q\ge1\), verify admissibility is equivalent to \(1\le i\le q\), \(1\le j\le r\), including \(s\le n-1\). Distinguish this from the noninjective map to the bare rectangle \(i^j\).

Under the stated boundary convention
\[
\{r\le5,\ q\le6\}\setminus\{r\le4,\ q\le5\},
\]
translate the 90 rectangular instances using the inverse formulas. Deduplicate through injectivity of the augmented correspondence. Retain the condition \(N>1\) as \(i\le q-1,\ j\le r-1\).

## Gaps
The boundary convention is a chosen interpretation, not canonically sourced. The rectangle \(i^j\) alone does not determine \(v_{r,s,t,n}\). The cited excerpt reports verification in the stated range but does not alone establish that no other verification range appears elsewhere. No minimality conclusion for the 90 translated cases follows from the correspondence or enumeration.

## Next
Present the two parametrized 60- and 30-case families as the conditional deduplicated translation. Keep minimality explicitly unresolved, except for separately certified finite examples.
